question: What kind of weather conditions are experienced as the distance from sea increases?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Extreme.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **distance from the sea** affects the **weather** conditions in a significant way. 
 
• The **farther away** from the sea, the **more extreme** the weather conditions become.
 
• When the distance from the sea** increases**, there is a** decrease **in the **moderating effect of the sea** on the climate, which results in extreme weather conditions.
 
• Extreme weather conditions can include **high temperatures, low temperatures, heavy precipitation**, and **strong winds.**
 
• The distance from the sea also affects the **humidity levels**, with inland areas experiencing lower humidity levels than coastal areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Light weather conditions **can be experienced in areas** closer to the sea**, where the moderating effect of the sea on the climate is stronger.

 
 
• Light weather conditions can include** mild temperatures, light precipitation, and gentle winds.**
 
 
 
• **Moderate **weather conditions can be experienced in areas that are** moderately far** from the sea.
 
 
• These areas may experience** moderate temperatures, moderate precipitation, and moderate winds**.
 
 
 
• The term** temperate **refers to a specific type of climate that is characterized by mild temperatures and moderate precipitation.
 
 
• Temperate climates are typically found in **areas closer to the sea,** where the moderating effect of the sea on the climate is stronger.
